euronews.description: In 27 regions of the Russian Federation, the immunodeficiency virus is spreading among the entire population, not only risk groups, according to the latest Rospotrebnadzor data. People increasingly pass the virus to one another, often unaware they are infected.

euronews.title: Why airlines are upgrading premium offerings in bid to boost profits
euronews.description: From a shared table in economy to a double bed in first class, airlines are finding new ways to sell passengers more premium space and amenities as higher fuel costs squeeze profits.

rfi.title: Drop in French food bank collection as rising cost of living hits donations
rfi.description: France’s annual food bank collection has gathered less than expected in the face of the rising cost of living which has left people with less money to spend on donations. The three-day campaign, which ended on Sunday, aimed to collect enough food to provide the equivalent of 20 million meals.

rfi.title: G7 talks in Paris weigh impact of US midterms on Trump's foreign policy
rfi.description: G7 foreign ministers are meeting in Paris on Monday, giving the world's top seven industrialised nations their first opportunity to assess how the US midterm elections may affect President Donald Trump's approach to Ukraine, the Middle East and relations with some of Washington's closest allies.

rfi.title: Cop31 opens in Turkey as climate funding and fossil fuels divide nations
rfi.description: United Nations climate talks get under way in Turkey on Monday, as the world heads beyond the 1.5C warming limit and poorer nations seek money to withstand floods and droughts, and countries remain divided over fossil fuels. Delegates from the United States will attend, but will not take part in negotiations.

rfi.title: Turkey courts Egypt to tip the scales in eastern Mediterranean power game
rfi.description: This week’s joint naval exercises between Turkey and Egypt in the eastern Mediterranean are the latest move in a burgeoning partnership, as Ankara intensifies its efforts to draw Cairo closer and loosen its bonds with Turkish rivals Greece, Cyprus and Israel.

rfi.title: French MPs weigh debate on banning conservative TV channel as petition tops 1m
rfi.description: A petition calling for French television channel CNews, often compared to US broadcaster Fox News, to be shut down has received over a million signatures, two days before lawmakers meet to consider whether a ban should be debated in parliament.

rfi.title: Spanish tennis star Alcaraz defeats Shelton to claim Paris Masters title

rfi.description: Gadi Eisenkot will on Sunday be formally given the chance to put together Israel's next government after elections on 27 October left neither of the main political parties with an overall majority.

rfi.title: Love story: literary speed dating in an age of declining readership
rfi.description: This week saw France hand out its biggest literary awards, the Prix Goncourt and the Prix Renaudot. However, reading is on the decline, with only 56 percent of French people describing themselves as regular readers in 2025, down 5 percentage points from 2023. But might those numbers rise if reading was a way to meet your soulmate?

rfi.title: French sailor Laperche sets record for Route du Rhum transatlantic sailing race
rfi.description: French sailor Tom Laperche set a record on his race debut to claim the Route du Rhum's Ultim class on Sunday.

rfi.title: Southern African farmers prepare for powerful El Nino with agroecology
rfi.description: Farmer Dudzai Matsapa works under a scorching sun, digging small, shallow pits across his field in Nyanga, east of the Zimbabwean capital, Harare. He will later fill these potholes with organic manure and wait for the rainy season. This is all part of Matsapa’s preparation for the anticipated El Nino, which is expected to trigger drought and extreme heat across southern Africa.

rfi.title: Bread shortage threatens to plunge more Sudanese into hunger
rfi.description: Nearly three and a half years into Sudan's unrelenting war, soaring costs and a nosediving currency have left people like Sawsan Mahmoud struggling to afford even the most basic staple – bread.

rfi.title: Poor facilities held back Senegal's medal-free Youth Olympics team, parents say
rfi.description: As the Youth Olympics continue in Dakar, parents of Senegal's young swimmers are calling for better training facilities and more government support after the country's team finished the competition without a medal.

rfi.title: The art of dressing: how clothes have shaped the image of the artist
rfi.description: How do you spot an artist? Are they the one with the jaunty beret or the dapper silk scarf? Or the tunic covered in paint? An exhibition at the Bourdelle Museum in Paris looks at how wardrobe choices have shaped society’s perception of artists – and made some of them into icons.

rfi.title: Nigeria's plan for state police raises hopes for security and fears of abuse
rfi.description: Nigeria this week took a step closer to a major overhaul of its security system after 28 of its 36 states approved a constitutional reform that would allow individual states to establish their own police forces. Supporters of the move say it will better protect against insecurity on a local level, but concerns have also been raised about the risk of abuse by state governors.

rfi.title: Mbappé returns to France duty as Zidane drafts Pagis into Nations League squad
rfi.description: France head coach Zinedine Zidane welcomed back skipper Kylian Mbappé into his squad for next week's Nations League games against Italy and Turkey and sprang a surprise with the selection of the 23-year-old Paris FC forward Pablo Pagis.

nzz.title: INTERAKTIV - So teuer ist Ihr Einkauf bei Aldi, Rewe und Co. geworden

nzz.description: Viel Raum und schnelle Ladezeiten: Der Hyptec HT zeigt, wie nahe chinesische Stromer der Oberklasse kommen.

nzz.title: DIE NEUESTEN ENTWICKLUNGEN - Migrationskrise in Europa: Mindestens 20 tote Migranten bei Schiffsunglücken vor Kreta

nzz.title: Bremsklotz Bürokratie: Schweizer Unternehmen klagen über eine stark steigende administrative Belastung
nzz.description: Eine Umfrage zeigt, dass zwei Drittel der Schweizer Firmen die Last durch Regulierungen als hoch empfinden. Offen bleibt, ob die neuen EU-Verträge das Problem verschärfen oder lindern würden.

nzz.title: Anschlag in Krakau: Die Staatsanwaltschaft stuft die Gewalttat als Terror ein. Der Täter ist tot
nzz.description: Polen trauert und steht unter Schock: Im Zentrum der zweitgrössten Stadt Polens hat ein junger Pole wahllos sechs Passanten erschossen. Er tötete zuvor seine Familie und soll laut dem Innenministerium rechtsextreme Ansichten vertreten.

nzz.title: KOMMENTAR - Europa braucht neue Prioritäten in der Klimapolitik
nzz.description: Die hohen Ziele der internationalen Klimakonferenzen sind gescheitert. Dennoch halten die europäischen Staaten stur an ihrem grünen Kurs fest. Es braucht eine flexiblere Ausrichtung der Energiepolitik.

nzz.title: INTERVIEW - Gerhard Pfister kritisiert vor der AHV-Abstimmung die FDP: «Zu suggerieren, es gehe ohne Mehreinnahmen, grenzt an bewusste Täuschung»
nzz.description: Die Mitte-Partei war gegen die Einführung der 13. AHV-Rente, nun kämpft sie für die Mehrwertsteuererhöhung. Im Interview erklärt ihr ehemaliger Präsident, wie die Politik die steigenden Sozialausgaben bezahlen will und warum er kein Sozialpopulist ist.

spiegel.title: Ilse Aigner: CDU-Vorstand schlägt CSU-Politikerin als Bundespräsidentin vor
spiegel.description: Der Abstimmungsprozess ist abgeschlossen, von SPD und Grünen kommt grünes Licht: Ilse Aigner wird von der Union als Präsidentschaftskandidatin aufgestellt. Sie kündigte an, eine Kandidatin der Mitte sein zu wollen.

spiegel.title: Ilse Aigner: Livestream zur offiziellen Vorstellung als Kandidatin für das höchste Staatsamt
spiegel.description: Erstmals soll eine Frau in Deutschland Bundespräsidentin werden: Bundeskanzler Friedrich Merz stellt die CSU-Politikerin Ilse Aigner offiziell als Kandidatin für das höchste Amt vor. Sehen Sie hier die Statements.

spiegel.title: Ukraine-Krieg: Ukraine und Russland attackieren sich vor Verhandlungen
spiegel.description: Am Dienstag verhandeln Russland und die Ukraine in den Emiraten erneut über ein mögliches Kriegsende. Kurz davor erhöhen beide Seiten mit gegenseitigen Angriffen den Druck.

spiegel.title: Vodafone streicht jede fünfte Stelle, setzt vermehrt auf KI
spiegel.description: Vodafone verlor zuletzt Marktanteile, nun legt der Konzern ein Sparprogramm auf. Zahlreiche Jobs sollen wegfallen oder verlagert werden. Aufgaben sollen stattdessen an KI ausgelagert werden.

spiegel.title: Wetter: Warmfront bringt Deutschland den Regen zurück
spiegel.description: »Intensivierenden Regen« kündigt der Deutsche Wetterdienst für die kommende Woche an. Die mildere Luft lässt zudem die Temperaturen steigen, mancherorts soll es bis zu 17 Grad warm werden.

spiegel.title: Arbeitsmarkt: KI hat laut Ifo-Auswertung Einfluss auf Berufschancen von Einsteigern
spiegel.description: In Berufsfeldern, in denen KI vor allem automatisiert, werden junge Beschäftigte seltener eingestellt als ältere. Das zeigt eine Auswertung des Ifo-Instituts. Dafür erstellten die Wissenschaftler ein Ranking von betroffenen Tätigkeiten.

spiegel.title: Donald Trump: UFC-Chef Dana White und seine politische Rolle für Trump
spiegel.description: Das Jobangebot als Pressesprecher soll nur ein »Scherz« gewesen sein, doch Donald Trump und Kampfsportfunktionär Dana White sind seit Jahren verbunden. Welche Rolle spielt White politisch für den US-Präsidenten?

spiegel.title: Jensen Huang: Hat Chinas Stasi den Nvidia-Chef in die Honigfalle gelockt?
spiegel.description: Pekings Geheimdienst MSS soll eine Agentin auf Nvidia-Boss Jensen Huang angesetzt haben. Die Spionage-Organisation ist Berichten zufolge »um ein Vielfaches größer« als die CIA.

spiegel.title: Quiz des Tages beim SPIEGEL: 7 Fragen zum Allgemeinwissen pro Tag
spiegel.description: Jeden Tag gibt es sieben Fragen zu den wichtigsten Themengebieten des politisch-gesellschaftlichen Geschehens. Testen Sie hier Ihr Wissen!

spiegel.title: Wagner zum 9. November: »Junge Menschen klettern in die Öfen des Krematoriums und zeigen das White-Power-Zeichen«
spiegel.description: Nach der Pogromnacht vom 9. November 1938 wurden 30.000 Juden in Konzentrationslager verschleppt. Historiker Jens-Christian Wagner erklärt, was mit ihnen geschah und wie Gedenkstätten von Provokateuren missbraucht werden.

spiegel.title: Ägypten: Mindestens sieben Menschen sterben bei Zugunglück
spiegel.description: Ein Zug ist südlich von Kairo auf einen anderen geprallt. Es gibt Tote und Verletzte. Die Ermittlungen zur Unglücksursache laufen.

spiegel.title: Nvidia: Aktie fällt nach Affären-Geständnis von Konzernchef Jensen Huang deutlich
spiegel.description: Der Seitensprung von Nvidia-Chef Jensen Huang und die möglichen Folgen für den Chipkonzern beschäftigen Anleger. Die Aktie gab deutlich nach. Der Dax dagegen stabilisierte sich.

spiegel.title: Biathlon: Franziska Preuß und Simon Schempp erwarten ein Kind
spiegel.description: Im Februar lief Franziska Preuß noch bei den Olympischen Winterspielen auf, danach beendete sie ihre Biathlon-Karriere. Nun gab sie bekannt, gemeinsam mit Olympiasieger Simon Schempp ein Kind zu erwarten.

spiegel.title: Elon Musk: Tesla wird offenbar nicht alle bestellten Cybertrucks ausliefern
spiegel.description: Der Cybertruck von Tesla hat den Massenmarkt nie erreicht. Nun werden offenbar viele Menschen, die das Ungetüm kaufen wollten, ihren Pick-up nie erhalten. Die Produktion soll laut Elon Musk Mitte 2027 eingestellt werden.

spiegel.title: Laser-Satellitenkommunikation: Bei dieser Weltraumtechnologie ist Deutschland weit vorn - noch
spiegel.description: Die Technik, um riesige Datenmengen per Laser über große Distanzen zu übertragen, wurde in Deutschland entwickelt. Genutzt wird sie jetzt primär von den USA. Experten fürchten, dass das Know-how ins Ausland abwandert.

spiegel.title: Claudia Roth: Antisemitismus-Netzwerk der Grünen kritisiert Politikerin
spiegel.description: 2024 wollte Claudia Roth nicht von »Genozid« und »Apartheid« im Gazastreifen und Westjordanland sprechen. Nun rückte sie in einem Podcast davon ab. Das stößt auch innerhalb ihrer Partei auf Kritik.

spiegel.title: USA: Donald Trump räumt Fehler bei Abschiebepolitik ein – »war zu hart«
spiegel.description: Die Klatsche bei den Midterms setzt den Republikanern noch immer zu. Im Bereich der Migrationspolitik zeigt sich Donald Trump nun reumütig, zumindest für den Moment.

spiegel.title: Nvidia: China weist Spionagevorwürfe gegen Jensen Huang zurück
spiegel.description: US-Sicherheitskreise vermuten, dass es sich bei einer Affäre des Nvidia-CEO Jensen Huang um eine chinesische Spionin handelt. Peking reagiert erbost und spricht von »Verleumdungen«.

observador.title: Os looks da red carped do LACMA 2026
observador.description: Na noite da Gucci, um vintage Pierre Cardin roubou a cena. De Nicole Kidman a Kim Kardashian, passando por Anya Taylor-Joy (pelas mãos de Law Roach), a passadeira vermelha fez-se de brilho e ousadia.

observador.description: Principais portos mundiais lançam rede internacional de combate ao tráfico de droga, que vai recorrer à IA para detetar mercadorias ilegais. Em Moçambique, IA ajuda a reforçar a cobertura vacinal.

observador.title: Tribunal suspende permanência de Renata Cambra no Rossio
observador.description: Com o efeito suspensivo declarado pelo tribunal, a manifestante Renata Cambra deixa de ter direito garantido a permanecer no Rossio. Mas o Tribunal Constitucional pode reverter a decisão.

observador.title: Polícia Judiciária apreende 4,5 toneladas de haxixe em Olhão
observador.description: A droga, escondida num veículo roubado, terá chegado ao terreno em Olhão por via marítima, através dos canais da Ria Formosa. Homem de 38 anos foi detido em flagrante delito.

observador.title: Acidente com três viaturas faz um ferido grave e corta EN118
observador.description: Acidente que envolveu um veículo ligeiro de passageiros, um ligeiro misto e um ligeiro de mercadorias provocou três feridos, um deles em estado grave. Estrada nacional mantém-se cortada ao trânsito.

observador.title: Arcos de Valdevez. Concurso para Centro para Nova Indústria
observador.description: Futuro polo tecnológico terá oito laboratórios dedicados à indústria avançada e à transição digital. Projeto resulta de uma parceria com a CiTin e conta com apoio do programa NORTE 2030.

observador.description: Reportagens, vídeos, podcasts e muito mais. Temos conteúdos sobre saúde, educação e inclusão no desporto. Dos amadores aos atletas. Dos clubes de bairro aos maiores. Todos importam.

observador.title: Parlamentos de Portugal e Moçambique alargam cooperação
observador.description: Acordo, que substitui o protocolo de cooperação parlamentar de 2017, prevê uma maior aposta na Assembleia Parlamentar da CPLP e um aumento da partilha de experiências tecnológicas e legislativas.

observador.title: Porto. Supremo reduz pena a homem que matou mulher à pancada
observador.description: Em janeiro passado, o arguido foi condenado, no Tribunal de São João Novo, no Porto, por um crime de homicídio, a 16 anos de prisão. Pena foi agora reduzida para 14 anos de prisão pelo Supremo.

observador.title: Ministro alemão rejeita nova ordem de segurança europeia
observador.description: Ministro dos Negócios Estrangeiros alemão reiterou que a Europa deve fazer parte da solução para a guerra na Ucrânia e ter voz nas negociações de um acordo de paz com a Rússia.

observador.title: Teerão anuncia inspeção da ONU à central nuclear de Bushehr
observador.description: Porta-voz do Ministério dos Negócios Estrangeiros do Irão diz que a representação iraniana em Viena mantém contactos "profissionais" e permanentes com a Agência Internacional de Energia Atómica.

observador.title: Creta. 20 migrantes encontrados mortos na costa em dois dias

public-dom.title: Philip Sidney and the Extreme (Dis)graces of the Parenthesis

public-dom.title: Artificial Intelligence: Ars Notoria and the Promise of Instant Knowledge

proj-syn.title: The Five Stages of AI Grief
proj-syn.description: Like those diagnosed with a terminal illness, humanity is being forced through the stages of denial, anger, bargaining, depression, and acceptance as AI’s capabilities and potential rapidly expand. But there is a crucial difference: AI and its uses are not outside our control.

proj-syn.title: The Economic Toll of Israel’s Wars
proj-syn.description: Israel’s economy may look strong, but three years of war have inflicted far greater damage than its robust stock market and appreciating currency suggest. Defense spending and government borrowing have risen sharply, while falling output and investment point to a prolonged recession.

proj-syn.title: Rebalancing Nature’s Books
proj-syn.description: The first report card on the implementation of the Kunming-Montreal framework was issued at this year’s UN Biodiversity Conference in Yerevan, and the marks were dismal. The problem is not a lack of targets, but a global financial system that pays to destroy nature and penalizes those who protect it.

proj-syn.title: Only Israel’s Arab Parties Can Restore Its Democracy
proj-syn.description: While Israel’s recent election did not deliver the transformation for which many might have hoped, it could open the way to restoring Israeli democracy. By building a coalition with the Arab-led parties, the opposition bloc could defeat not only Benjamin Netanyahu but also the violent, racist ideology he embodies.

proj-syn.title: Making the Most of America’s Midterm Tsunami
proj-syn.description: American voters’ demand for the rule of law and democracy has helped destroy Trump’s MAGA movement. Affordability may have ranked first among their concerns, but addressing it will depend on repairing and improving democratic institutions.

proj-syn.title: AI Can Help Governments Help Citizens
proj-syn.description: In developing economies, the AI debate has focused less on frontier risk and more on how to ensure that the technology actually serves people. That will require not only designing AI tools to work within government, but also investing in the state capacity required to put the technology to use.

proj-syn.title: MAGA’s Midterm Defeat Won’t Change the Course of History
proj-syn.description: The world must not succumb to euphoria following Donald Trump’s latest defeat. If anything, his lame-duck status deprives Americans and everyone else of an excuse for avoiding hard conversations about the truly radical changes that will be needed to avert future catastrophes.

proj-syn.title: Can AI Colonialism Be Prevented?
proj-syn.description: As the United States and China cement their technological dominance, the AI revolution threatens to reproduce the colonial dynamics of the first Industrial Revolution. To avoid digital colonization, middle powers must work together to build an open AI stack and establish common standards to govern it.

proj-syn.title: Turning Sub-Saharan Africa’s Cities Into Job Engines
proj-syn.description: Cities and towns will be central to creating more and better jobs for Sub-Saharan Africa’s fast-growing population, simply because the region’s people and economic activity are increasingly concentrated there. But unlocking urbanization’s potential requires policy guidance and well-planned investment.

proj-syn.title: Why Are Indian Protesters Targeting the Electoral Commission?
proj-syn.description: Following a “special intensive revision” that struck 130 million voters from the electoral rolls, India’s youth have mounted large-scale protests against the Election Commission. Given the convergence of protests with the formal political opposition, the Commission is unlikely to avoid accountability for mass disenfranchisement.

proj-syn.title: Why Aren’t We Investing More in Climate Adaptation?
proj-syn.description: There are many proven ways to protect people and assets from extreme weather, and such measures often prevent economic losses worth many times their cost. But ensuring their implementation requires making them more affordable and creating innovative revenue mechanisms and financing structures.

proj-syn.title: Put the Ocean at the Center of COP31
proj-syn.description: Last year’s UN Climate Change Conference in Belém, Brazil, put forests high on the climate agenda. This month’s UN Climate Change Conference in Antalya, Turkey, can do the same for the ocean, whose warming threatens not just food and energy security but global survival.

proj-syn.title: Who’s Winning (and Who’s Losing) the Ocean?
proj-syn.description: Ahead of COP31, PS sat down with Peter Thomson, the UN Secretary-General's Special Envoy for the Ocean, to discuss the logic of “blue” economic development. Watch as he warns of a “world on fire,” takes governments to task for kowtowing to the oil and gas industry, and explains how we can do better for future generations.

proj-syn.title: The Democrats’ Historic Duty
proj-syn.description: While Democrats have good reason to celebrate their historic midterm victory, their current elation must quickly harden into determination. Fortunately, the field for new ideas, systemic and economic, in the US will be the most open it is likely to be for decades.

proj-syn.title: Dot-Com Lessons for the AI Bubble
proj-syn.description: Anyone who lived through the internet boom and bust of the late 1990s and early 2000s should find the current AI investment cycle worryingly familiar. Heavy reliance on debt means that if investors decide to stop lending into the boom, a financial crisis will be inevitable—and far worse than the subprime-mortgage crisis in 2008.

proj-syn.title: China Is Defanging the Dollar, Not Dethroning It
proj-syn.description: China offers Iran and Russia a way to circumvent US sanctions and continue doing business. But this comes at an elevated cost, because these countries are paid in onshore, non-convertible renminbi, which they must then convert into dollars using underground financial networks—tacitly reinforcing the greenback’s dominance.

proj-syn.title: A Fatal Challenge to Mainstream Economics
proj-syn.description: The intellectual project on which mainstream economists were raised, and which still forms the backbone of textbook education, has disappeared. What remains is a pastiche of attempted patches, apologies, and corruptions of “heterodox” ideas, all peddled by exponents of an “orthodoxy” that lacks a theoretical core.

proj-syn.title: The ECB Must Bail Out France
proj-syn.description: If France is to avoid default, the European Central Bank will need to buy large amounts of its government’s bonds through the Transmission Protection Instrument. But meeting this need—and preventing a potentially disastrous eurozone sovereign-debt-crisis—will require the ECB to waive its own rules.
